problem: int(amount.scaleb(places)) silently cuts off digits past `places` instead of raising, so shares no longer add up to the amount ("10.005",[1,1] -> 5.00+5.00).
`sum(ws) or Fraction(1)` replaces a zero weight total with 1, so zero-sum weights give shares that don't add up to the amount ([0,0] -> 0.01+0.01 of 10; [1,-1] -> 10.01,-9.99).
Weight checks were removed, so negative and zero weights give negative or overpaid shares ([2,-1] -> 20.00,-10.00) and an empty list returns [] with no error.
Negative amounts are no longer rejected and are split into negative shares ("-0.01",[1,1] -> 0.00,-0.01).
Decimal(str(x)) replaces _to_decimal and accepts float amounts and weights that main rejected with TypeError, and their rounding noise is then silently cut off.
`places` is no longer checked: negative values return exponent-notation results that lose money ("155",places=-1 -> total 150) and True is treated as 1.

Bad inputs (NaN, Infinity, None, bool) now raise decimal.InvalidOperation, OverflowError or ValueErrors with internal messages instead of main's ValueError/TypeError naming the argument, so callers catching those miss them.
`max(leftover, 0)` hides a negative leftover, so a total that no longer matches the amount comes back as a normal-looking result instead of failing.
The rework ships with no tests, so a check that the shares add up to the amount, plus one test per rejected input, would have caught F1-F4.
_to_decimal is now dead code and describes an input contract that allocate no longer enforces.
The comment documenting the largest-remainder, lowest-index tie-break was removed, though the rule still decides who gets the extra unit.
